title: Cotransport of nanoscale zero-valent iron and electroactive bacteria in saturated porous media: impacts of bacterial extracellular electron transfer and energy taxis
content: Nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI) is increasingly incorporated into bioremediation to enhance remediation efficiency. However, the cotransport behaviors of nZVI and electroactive bacteria in porous media remain largely unexplored. This study revealed that the cotransport of Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and nZVI in porous media was significantly impeded by extracellular electron transfer (EET)-driven interactions. Assays involving mutant strains, altered solution chemistry, and varying hydrodynamic conditions demonstrated that the active taxis of MR-1 toward nZVI promoted their dense heteroaggregation and subsequent deposition in porous media. Furthermore, barriers formed on nZVI surfaces by carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) coating and natural aging physically blocked interfacial electron transfer, thereby suppressing energy taxis and enhancing cotransport. In contrast, sulfidation of nZVI constructed a highly conductive FeSx layer that hyper-activated EET and energy taxis, exacerbating heteroaggregation and restricting cotransport. These results emphasized that EET-driven responses could overcome physicochemical repulsions, necessitating the consideration of microbial metabolic activities when optimizing nZVI deployment for in situ bioremediation.
